original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: #2277 open question 4 (E6 / D5 realisation-free): is the Gram point G of the rank-<=T realisation variety (M_tt != 0, M_ts = 0 for orthogonal t,s) rigid up to diagonal scalings D1 G D2 for E6 (v=36, T=6) and D5 (v=20, T=5), and does the dense-pairing floor of #2277 survive on non-Gram realisations?
scope_change_reason: The generic rank-shape card is crowded by masked/overcomplete decoder searches (#2430, #2338, #2240, #2247, #2232, #2137). #2277 proves E6 >= 36 and D5 >= 20 only for scaled-Gram realisations and lists rigidity of the Gram point as open; a non-Gram rank-T realisation is a decoder geometry outside those floors (Theorem 4' gives nothing because E6/D5 have no T-frame). This is a structural decoder question (seed 49, track 40-49), not a per-call profile, so the card's 5% ceiling gate does not apply.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the complex decoder floor programme: it closes (locally, at rank T) the realisation loophole of the #2277 E6 36 / D5 20 floors. It is not a per-call profile, frontier unit or supplier change; no kappa claim.
stop_rule: Stop when (A) E6 tangent dimension and (B) the D5 family are exact and the controls pass; one bounded pivot (C) limited to the D5 family (explicit points plus a symbolic span lemma), no rank-5 E6 search.
evidence: verify.py (stdlib, exact; ~8 s, 42 checks; 43 with --e8): E6 dim T_G V = 71 = 2v-1 (prime-rank upper bound at two primes and in a second coordinate model, matched by the explicit scaling-orbit span) => G smooth, local component = scaling orbit (local rigidity). E7 125 = 2v-1 control (E8 239 = 2v-1 behind --e8). D5: tangent 55 = 39 + 16, explicit 16-parameter non-Gram family; written proofs that D5 has no rank-4 realisation (Theorem E) and that every rank-5 realisation is edge-supported (Theorem D, construction replayed exactly on 5 instances incl. a boundary member); on every edge-supported realisation the deficient classes are the 5 axis classes, so #2277's floor 20 holds for every rank-<=5 realisation of D5 and is attained. Controls D4 44>23 exact (edge family only 32, exact), D6 84 = edge family; negative controls fail as required.

open_questions.question: Global uniqueness at rank 6 for E6: is every rank-6 realisation of E6 of the form D1 G D2 (not only those near G)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would make #2277's E6 >= 36 realisation-free at rank T, closing the non-Gram loophole for square decoders.

open_questions.blocked_by: No frame argument (alpha_perp = 4); the local certificate here says nothing about other components.
